It is a free, paperless, self-declaration portal linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.
x: Udyam Registration, introduced in 2020, is free, paperless and based on self-declaration; it is linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.

s: Which institution supports the RAMP programme for strengthening MSME institutions, market access and credit?
x: RAMP is a World Bank-supported programme to strengthen Centre-State MSME institutions, market access and credit.

s: In the case of a non-individual enterprise under Stand-Up India, eligibility requires that at least what shareholding and control be with SC/ST persons or women?
x: A non-individual enterprise qualifies when at least 51 per cent of its shareholding and control is held by SC/ST persons or women.

s: Stand-Up India, launched in April 2016, supports which kind of enterprise?
x: Stand-Up India supports only greenfield (new) enterprises promoted by SC/ST persons or women. It is not a rehabilitation scheme for sick units, does not fund expansion of existing units, and has nothing to do with disinvestment of PSEs.

s: How many trades does PM Vishwakarma cover, and what credit does it offer?
o: 12 trades, with credit up to ₹3 lakh at 7% interest
24 trades, with credit up to ₹5 lakh at 4% interest
18 trades, with credit up to ₹10 lakh at 5% interest
18 trades, with credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5% interest
x: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 trades and provides credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest.

s: Which agency implements the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
x: PMEGP, a credit-linked margin-money subsidy scheme for new micro-enterprises, is implemented by KVIC, not NABARD.

s: In which year was the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) launched?
x: PMEGP came in 2008, a year after the Ministry of MSME (2007); Stand-Up India followed in 2016 and Udyam Registration in 2020.

s: Under Startup India, an entity is recognised for up to how many years from incorporation?
x: DPIIT recognises entities up to 10 years old; deep-tech startups up to 20 years.

s: For what does MSE-CDP mainly provide grants?
x: MSE-CDP is cluster development with grants for common facility centres.

s: What does the Self-Reliant India Fund (2021) provide to MSMEs?
x: The Self-Reliant India Fund (2021) gives equity to MSMEs through daughter funds.

s: PMEGP was formed by merging PMRY with which scheme?
x: PMEGP (2008) is PMRY plus REGP.

s:
Consider the following statements about Stand-Up India:
1. It was launched in April 2018.
2. It supports greenfield units.
3. Its beneficiaries are SC/ST persons or women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Stand-Up India (April 2016, not 2018) supports greenfield units of SC/ST persons or women.

s: What is the size of the SME Growth Fund announced in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Budget 2026-27 announced a ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund for 'Champion MSMEs'.

s: What is the revised turnover limit for an entity to be recognised as a startup under Startup India?
x: The turnover limit was raised from ₹100 crore to ₹200 crore; ₹300 crore applies to deep-tech startups.

s: Under PMEGP, up to what rate of margin-money subsidy can women beneficiaries get?
x: PMEGP gives special categories such as women a subsidy of up to 35%.

s: For up to how many years from incorporation can a deep-tech entity be recognised as a startup under Startup India?
x: Ordinary startups are recognised up to 10 years; deep-tech startups up to 20 years (turnover up to ₹300 crore).

s: What daily stipend is paid during training under PM Vishwakarma?
x: PM Vishwakarma pays artisans in 18 trades a stipend of ₹500 per day during training.

s: For whom does the MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 make settlement of MSME invoices through TReDS mandatory?
x: The MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 makes TReDS settlement mandatory for CPSEs.

s: Disputes relating to delayed payments to micro and small enterprises are referred to which body?
x: Disputes concerning delayed payments are referred to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.

s: Under Chapter V of the MSMED Act, within how many days must a buyer pay an MSE supplier?
x: Chapter V requires payment within 45 days, beyond which compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate is payable.

s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012, central ministries and CPSEs are required to procure what minimum share of their annual procurement from MSEs?
x: The mandatory procurement share from MSEs is 25 per cent; it was raised from 20 per cent in 2018.

s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, what is the sub-target for procurement from women-owned MSEs?
x: The sub-targets are 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs and 4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs.

s: If a buyer delays payment to an MSE supplier, at what rate must it pay compound interest?
o: Three times the RBI bank rate
Four times the RBI bank rate
x: Section 16 of the MSMED Act prescribes compound interest at 3 times the RBI bank rate.

s: Under the Public Procurement Policy, what is the sub-target for SC/ST-owned MSEs?
x: The sub-targets are 4% for SC/ST-owned and 3% for women-owned MSEs.

s: From what level was the procurement target from MSEs raised to 25% in 2018?
x: Ministries and CPSEs must buy 25% from MSEs, raised from 20% in 2018.

s: In FY26 (up to 1 December 2025), what share of procurement by central ministries and CPSEs came from MSEs?
x: Against the 25% target, procurement from MSEs reached 44.76% in FY26 (to 1 Dec 2025).
